name: happy
description:
Four Orion nodes through one SWIS query.

The scenario exists because this integration shipped with `params = {'query': ''}` -- it asked the Information Service for nothing and therefore imported nothing, on every run, silently. request_include pins the SWQL actually reaching the wire so an empty query cannot come back.

Identity is the other half. build_assets falls back NodeId -> Fqdn -> IpAddress, so node 3 carries no NodeId and must key on its Fqdn, and node 4 carries neither and must key on its address. Node 5 has none of the three and must be counted, not imported: it is the only record the skip line may describe.

network_interface returns None when nothing usable survives, and appending that aborts the whole run at ImportAsset, so node 3's empty IpAddress is deliberate -- it proves the guard holds and the asset still imports on hostname alone.

IDS ARE NAMESPACED BY THE SWIS SERVER. Orion's NodeId is a small per-install integer and Fqdn and IpAddress are unique only inside one installation, so a bare id collides as soon as two Orion servers are imported into one runZero account -- with integers counting from 1 that is close to certain. The id therefore carries the configured URL's host, which is the only thing distinguishing the two that this API exposes. $HOST expands to the fixture server's host so the scoped ids can still be asserted exactly against an ephemeral port.
